newsitem.title: UAE: Air cargo leader seeks consultation on US security.
newsitem.headline: Air cargo leader seeks consultation on US security.

text.p: The president of the International Air Cargo Association (TIACA) expressed concern Sunday over new U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) security rules for air cargo, which he said were issued without any input or involvement from the industry.
Speaking at the opening in Dubai of an association conference, TIACA president Ram Menen acknowledged that "TIACA must back all reasonable measures to counteract terrorism."

But Menem, who is also senior general manager, cargo for Emirates Airlines, added: "With the input of all the components of the air cargo industry, equally effective and less damaging security measures could be identified."
The four-day TIACA conference includes leaders of the world air cargo industry, fairlines, freight forwarders, airports and exporters.

"The inevitable consequence is that the regulations, far from securing the industry, could well seriously damage it. The new FAA security rules, issued without any industry input will continue to ensure that the air cargo vehicle may never get out first gear," he said.
Separately he said that he favored multi-modal solutions as the answer to maximizing profits among shippers, forwarders and other industry players.

"To achieve this, the industry now has to form alliances. We must create system of seamless, multi-modal transportation, " he said with billing and tracking documentation common to all transport systems.
